title: Submit a run input
description: Submit a run of a runbook: its intake (inline), its context (a path under a daemon context root), its settings and its confinement (optional: a submit that names none runs at the daemon's default level; a daemon with none refuses it by name, and nothing is written), and optionally an autonomy level and a decider kind (a submit that names none takes the daemon's defaults; a kind the operator did not configure, or a level with no kind to take it, is refused before anything is written and creates no run), into a session or alone. The run is Submitted; the runtime starts it. The accepted outcome (submitted) also makes the daemon write the run's first event: kind `runbook.submitted`, sequence 1, record {run_id, runbook_id, confinement, confinement_source, and autonomy, decider, model_route, model_route_alias and model_route_source when the run has them}, and the next position of the daemon; the run's next sequence starts at 2, so the first event the runtime records for the run is sequence 2 (RecordRunEvent). A replayed submit (already-submitted) writes no event and creates no run; a refused submit (every error outcome) creates no run and writes none. The language cannot write a RunEvent from this command (an outcome creates or moves rows of one entity), so this is stated here and in the summaries of the daemon's other own events, and read through the event views only: the interpreted target keeps no row for it and accepts sequence 1, the daemon refuses it as not ascending. The daemon mints the run id and the HTTP handler fills `run_id` and `daemon_id`; a client never chooses them. A client that wants a safe retry sends an `idempotency_key`: a second submit with a key already used returns the first run and creates none (outcome already-submitted, answered with the first run). The handler also reports three facts it reads from the host, because the language cannot read a file system: `runbook_known`, `context_inside_roots` and the size of the inline intake (checked here); the checks themselves are outside the language and are tested in the story daemon-skeleton-on-a-runtime-trait. The client names no daemon: `daemon_id` is an input because a guard that reads the Daemon row through a row set cannot be synthesized (ESS-SYNTH-001), while `via` plus `predicate` can. The floor guard spells the order of the two levels out, one outcome for the one floor that refuses something, because the ordered comparison `confinement_floor > input.confinement` validates but the interpreted target then accepts every level (a defect of the interpreted target of ESS 0.96.0); the outcome changes with the level names. A run that makes model calls (its decider is a model at a level above A0, or its runbook runs a bound program or an agent node, which reaches a model through the run's route file) takes a model route (docs/model-routes.md, sections 2 and 11): the one the submit names by name in `model_route` (and per role in `model_routes`), then the route its runbook's route entries give the role (`bindings/<runbook>.routes.yaml`, format runbook.routes/1: a declared route by name, or needs that the run's route or the default meets, else the one allowed route that meets them), else the daemon's `route_policy.default`; every route of the run lies within the entries' routes_allowed; the handler resolves it against the routes the daemon's file declares, fills `model_route`, `model_route_alias` and `model_route_source`, and reports a route it refuses in the fact `route_refused` before anything is written. The route is recorded on the run; the runtime sends every model call of the run through the daemon's relay to that route's gateway, with the route's alias as the model. Before anything is written the handler also asks the gateway of each route of the run the daemon's file declares (`GET /ready`, `GET /v1/models` and the status of the model; docs/model-routes.md, section 3): a gateway that is not ready or does not answer refuses the submit with the HTTP status 503 `route-unavailable`, outside this specification like the 503 of a submit while the daemon drains (no outcome of the language has that status), and one that does not list the route's alias refuses it route-refused; a route whose model cannot answer yet leaves the run accepted, and the daemon holds it WaitingForRoute (WaitForRoute). The interim route `default` of a daemon with a lone `[gateway]` and no route of its own is not asked, as before routes, nor is a submit that repeats an idempotency key already used: it is answered already-submitted with the first run. No wake is sent before the run is written: a run held WaitingForRoute may wake a managed route whose wake is on (WaitForRoute). A submit may name a `serial_key` (1 to 200 characters, the submitter's; the daemon never derives one, and an empty or a longer key is refused before anything is written, 400): the run is recorded with it, `runbook.submitted` names it, and while a run with the same key submitted before it holds the key (it is live, or the runtime took it up and has not let it go yet) the daemon holds the run WaitingOnKey (WaitOnKey) and takes it up once none holds it (TakeKey); runs with another key or none are not held.

confinement.description: The level the client named; absent when it named none, and the run then takes the daemon's default level (a daemon with none refuses the submit by name; the handler fills it and says which in confinement_source).

confinement_source.description: Where the level came from: the handler fills it. A client never sends it.

autonomy.description: The autonomy level of the run, A0 to A5: how much of its decisions a decider takes over from a person. Absent: the daemon's default level, and when it has none every decision of the run waits for a client.

decider.description: The kind of the decider that answers what the level gives it, a name among the kinds the operator configured. Absent: the daemon's default kind. A kind that is not configured, and a level with no kind to take it, are refused before anything is written (400).

serial_key.description: The serial key of the run: runs with one key run one at a time, in submit order. Absent: the run is not held for any other.

model_route.description: The route of the run's role `default`, by the name the daemon's file declares it under; never an address, a token or a gateway's alias, each refused by name. Absent: the daemon's `route_policy.default` for a run that makes model calls, through its decider (a model above A0) or its programs (a bound program or an agent node of its runbook, which reach a model through the run's route file; the handler fills it and says which in model_route_source; a run whose model calls come from its programs only takes it only when the file declares it and the daemon serves its relay, else none), none for a run that makes none. A run that makes no model call and names a route is refused (route-refused).

model_routes.description: The route of each further role of the run, by name, under the same rules as model_route.

model_route_alias.description: The alias of model_route at its gateway: the handler fills it from the daemon's file. A client never sends it.

model_route_source.description: Where model_route came from: the handler fills it. A client never sends it.

route_refused.description: Why the handler refuses the run's route, when it does: a fact it reads from the daemon's file, which the language cannot read. Absent when the route is admitted or the run takes none. A client never sends it.

sdc.daemon.ConfinementLevel.title: ConfinementLevel
sdc.daemon.ConfinementLevel.description: How strongly a run is sandboxed, weakest first: the runtime's names. local is not confined; linux is. oci and pod are the runtime's planned levels and are not in the set until it offers them. A submit that names no level runs at the daemon's default level (runbook serve --default-confinement, or `confinement` of runbook.toml); a daemon with none refuses the submit by name and writes nothing, as the binary has no built-in default; the handler fills it. The daemon's floor is linux unless it is started lower; the default is never below the floor, and a daemon whose default is below its floor does not start. local must be asked for by name or set as the default, and is refused under a linux floor.

sdc.daemon.ConfinementSource.title: ConfinementSource
sdc.daemon.ConfinementSource.description: Where a run's level came from: submit (the client named it) or daemon-default (the client named none and the daemon's default level applied). There is no third source: a daemon with no default refuses a submit that names none.

sdc.daemon.ContextPath.title: ContextPath
sdc.daemon.ContextPath.description: A directory on the daemon's host, given as an absolute path. The daemon accepts it only when it lies under one of its context roots (runbook serve --context-root <dir>, repeatable; none given means no context from a path), and copies it into the run's workspace before the run starts.

sdc.daemon.DaemonId.title: DaemonId
sdc.daemon.DaemonId.description: The id of the one daemon the specification describes: the configuration row it holds is keyed by it. The HTTP handler fills it; one process is one daemon.

sdc.daemon.DeciderKind.title: DeciderKind
sdc.daemon.DeciderKind.description: The name of a decider kind the operator configured (a table [deciders.<kind>] of runbook.toml): rule or model. A run names a kind, never a program or a path; a kind that is not configured is refused at the submit before anything is written.

sdc.daemon.IdempotencyKey.title: IdempotencyKey
sdc.daemon.IdempotencyKey.description: Optional text, at most 200 characters, unique per daemon, that a client sends to retry a submit safely: a second submit with a key already used returns the first run and creates none.

sdc.daemon.RoleRoutes.title: RoleRoutes
sdc.daemon.RoleRoutes.description: The route of each named role of a run (`writer`, `review`, ...) besides the role `default`: a role is the word a model process of the run names as its model, and the daemon's relay sends the call to the role's route. A role and a route are each one to 64 characters of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`; a role does not start with `runbook-`, the prefix of the model the run's route file gives a role.

sdc.daemon.RouteName.title: RouteName
sdc.daemon.RouteName.description: The name of a model route the daemon declares (a table [routes.<name>] of its runbook.toml): one to 64 characters of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`. A client names a route by it, never by an address, a token or an alias; the address, the token file and the prices stay in the daemon's file.

sdc.daemon.RouteSource.title: RouteSource
sdc.daemon.RouteSource.description: The setting that chose a run's route: run (the submit named it, `model_route` or `model_routes.<role>`), protocol (the runbook's route entries, the file `bindings/<runbook>.routes.yaml` of format runbook.routes/1: the route its entry for the role names, or the route that meets the entry's needs; docs/model-routes.md section 2) or default (the submit named none and the daemon's `route_policy.default` applied; a daemon whose file declares no route but a lone `[gateway]` table and a model decider declares the interim route `default` on that gateway and takes it as its default, so a model run that names none says default too). The run's word comes first, then the protocol's, then the default.

sdc.daemon.RunId.title: RunId
sdc.daemon.RunId.description: The id of a run. The daemon mints it (a UUID, version 7) in the HTTP handler and returns it in the answer to the submit; the handler fills the `run_id` input of SubmitRun and a client never chooses it. The state directory of the run is named after it. A run id that is already taken cannot occur, because the daemon mints it; the specification has no refusal for it.

sdc.daemon.RunSettings.title: RunSettings
sdc.daemon.RunSettings.description: The settings of a run: a map from text to text (runbook run --set key=value), kept as written. Typed members come with the runtime's run-settings story; none are declared now.

sdc.daemon.RunbookId.title: RunbookId
sdc.daemon.RunbookId.description: The name of a runbook: a preset (sdc, sdc-bugfix) or the name of a runbook in the daemon's --runbook-dir.

sdc.daemon.RunbookVersion.title: RunbookVersion
sdc.daemon.RunbookVersion.description: The version of a runbook, as runbook list shows it. Optional in a submit: absent means the version the daemon has.

sdc.daemon.SerialKey.title: SerialKey
sdc.daemon.SerialKey.description: Optional text, 1 to 200 characters, that the submitter names (the daemon never derives one): runs with one key run one at a time, in the order they were submitted. A run whose key a run submitted before it holds is WaitingOnKey until no such run holds it: a live run holds it, and a run that was taken up holds it until its run thread in the daemon has returned, also after it was Cancelled; runs with another key or none are not held. A key that is empty or longer is refused before anything is written (400).

sdc.daemon.SessionId.title: SessionId
sdc.daemon.SessionId.description: The name of a session, chosen by the client that opens it.

sdc.decision.AutonomyLevel.title: AutonomyLevel
sdc.decision.AutonomyLevel.description: The run's autonomy level, docs/autonomy-levels.md:36-42 and :205-213: A0 Manual, A1 Advised, A2 Internal, A3 To merge, A4 To release, A5 Unattended (eval runs, :41-42). The level does not decide eligibility by itself: with the request's decision class it gives the holder (:241-256, overrides :297-320), and the guards read the holder.
